abstract: We establish optimal sheet separation estimates for stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions up to seven, using an iteration argument in the nonlocal approximation theory of Chan-Dipierro-Serra-Valdinoci. These estimates imply that every stable $s$-minimal hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a hyperplane when $s$ is close to $1$. More generally, every finite Morse index $s$-minimal set in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a half-space. We also establish a compactness theorem for stable $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$. We prove uniform curvature and area estimates for their links and show that, as $s \uparrow 1$, they subconverge graphically in $C^{2,\alpha}$, either with multiplicity one to a classical stable minimal cone, or with multiplicity two to a hyperplane. The stability of Lawson and axisymmetric $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$ shows that these results are optimal.
hook: Stable s-minimal hypersurfaces in 7 dimensions are flat when s is near 1, and 8 dimensions is the limit
summary: The authors prove sheet separation estimates showing every stable s-minimal hypersurface in R^7 is a hyperplane for s near 1. In R^8 they prove a compactness result for stable cones, which converge to classical minimal cones or a doubled hyperplane. Known examples show the dimension cutoff cannot be improved.
title: Stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions seven and eight
